218556148_72cf6fbb.text: Amid the first areas of the CNS that were found to be sexually dimorphic are regions regulating reproductive behaviors, such as the medial preoptic area (mPOA) and the anteroventral periventricular nucleus (AVPV) of the hypothalamus (Simerly, 2002). However, differences in the size of brain nuclei, number of cells and connectivity have been found in other regions of the brain not directly involved with reproductive behaviors, such as the hippocampus (Zhang et al., 2008), the locus coeruleus (LC) (Guillamón et al., 1988), the amygdala and other limbic regions (Simerly, 2002)(Cooke et al., 1999). The LC is a noradrenergic nucleus of the brainstem that is involved in arousal, vigilance, attention, cognition and the stress response (Berridge et al., 2003)(Charmandari et al., 2005) (Sara, 2009)

218556148_beccf1aa.text: The medial preoptic area (mPOA) of the hypothalamus is a sexually dimorphic area that regulates sex behaviors in males [28,29] and maternal behavior [30].
